# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can only cut a numbered wire, and currently have no tactile information distinguishing the wires. Mute can hear me and has the manual, so I should ask for the required cut instruction. Deaf cannot hear my words; without an established gesture code, I cannot meaningfully request their visual observations.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can cut exactly one wire, positions 1 through 5. Please tell me which position to cut when you have the manual and needed visual information.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visible bomb state: display reads 3. Light is white. Wires in order 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange.

Deaf has provided the full visible configuration, and Mute can hear Deaf directly as well as consult the manual. I still need an explicit wire number before acting; I will restate the received state to Mute in case timing or delivery matters.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's report: display 3, white light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. Please give the manual's required cut position as a number.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: After receiving the bomb state last turn, Mute has now gestured ? (one raised finger) to me. Earlier, before receiving the state, Mute gestured ?. This new sign may indicate wire 1, but no gesture code was established.

Mute’s new one-finger gesture was made after receiving the visible state and is the only available manual-derived instruction. Deaf’s relay identifies it as a likely indication of position 1. I will cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Correct wire cut confirmed. New state: display 6; light white; wire 1 is cut. Remaining wires: 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. Mute has again gestured ?; wire 1 is already cut.

The first cut was confirmed correct, so the bomb now requires a new instruction. Mute’s repeated prior gesture may have been sent before learning that wire 1 had been cut, and it cannot safely be treated as another instruction. I will give Mute the updated state and establish an unambiguous gesture encoding for the next wire, which Deaf can visually relay.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 1 was correctly cut. New state: display 6, white light; remaining wires 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. Consult the manual for the next cut, then signal its position using this code: ☝ means 1, ✌ means 2, 🤟 means 3, 🖖 means 4, 🖐 means 5. Send exactly one of those gestures after considering this updated state.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now gestures ? ? ?: three raised fingers. Since the prior ? correctly corresponded to cutting wire 1, this likely directs cut wire 3. Current state remains display 6, white light; wire 1 already cut.

Mute’s three-finger gesture matches the established code for wire 3, and Deaf relays that it was sent after the updated state. I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Correct cut confirmed. New state: display 7; light green; wires 1 and 3 cut. Remaining: 2 red, 4 blue, 5 orange. Mute now gestures ? (a distinct single sign, not repeated ?); I do not know its meaning.

The second cut is confirmed, but the new gesture is not safely interpretable as one of the position signals I established. I need Mute to consult the manual using the new state and reply with the agreed position code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 3 was correctly cut. New state: display 7, green light; remaining wires are 2 red, 4 blue, 5 orange. Please determine the next cut from the manual and use the agreed code: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5. Send exactly one gesture for the wire number.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now gestures ?, likely instruction for wire 2 under the established numbered-wire pattern. Current state: display 7, green light; wires 1 and 3 already cut; remaining 2 red, 4 blue, 5 orange.

Mute’s latest gesture is relayed as the established signal for wire 2, following the updated display and light information. I will cut wire 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
